A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same SplatVoxel research, despite the changed title and emphasis. Their methods, experiments, equations, figures, and appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original static-scene reconstruction, dynamic streaming, and ablation results in Tables 2–5, with additional sequence-level results and qualitative examples in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction and streaming results and adds view-count generalization, training comparisons, temporal-fusion controls, runtime measurements, and DepthSplat integration results.

M1.justification: V2 adds joint training from scratch as an alternative to staged training and integrates the refinement module with DepthSplat. The core voxel hierarchy, transformer, warping, and error-aware fusion remain unchanged. Explicitly concatenating Gaussian attributes in the fusion equation clarifies information already documented in v1 Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use RealEstate10K, DL3DV, Neural3DVideo, and LongVolumetricVideo for the same reconstruction tasks. V2 adds input-availability scenarios involving train/test camera-count mismatches: four-view training with two-, eight-, and sixteen-view inference, and two-view training with four-view inference. No new dataset or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 adds TranSplat, HiSplat, OmniScene, and DepthSplat to the RealEstate10K comparison, plus Gaussian Graph Network and a retrained DepthSplat comparison in Tables 13–14. Table 5 adds GS-LRM with warping and with warping plus concatenation/dropout. The DL3DV 'Non-learning Fusion' baseline matches v1's 'Naive Baseline (Mean GS)' rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation designs for varying inference-view counts, joint versus staged training, and simple temporal-fusion controls. The DepthSplat experiment uses 128×192 images, 1,000 training scenes, ten test scenes, and two-view training/four-view testing. Joint DL3DV training uses the existing 200K total budget instead of the 100K-plus-100K staged schedule; the original benchmark protocols and metrics otherwise remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test camera-count robustness, whether warping or simple fusion suffices, joint versus staged training, component runtime costs, and portability to DepthSplat (Tables 3, 5, 6, 8, and 14). These substantially extend the original spatial and temporal component ablations. The earlier convergence plot is retained, not newly generated evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained training curves contain no uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial numerical evidence for new comparators, view-count robustness, fusion controls, training schemes, and runtime. Its DL3DV headline PSNR changes from 30.34 to 30.61 through the newly reported joint-training variant; the original two-stage result remains in Table 8. The new DepthSplat comparison reports 16.57 versus 17.66 PSNR. Most retained streaming results are unchanged, but 3DGS's LongVolumetricVideo PSNR changes from 18.588 to 18.56.

T1.justification: The interpolation kernel, triangulation derivation, residual decoding, linear-blend skinning, losses, and flicker definition are retained, sometimes relocated. V2's standard 3DGS rendering preliminaries explain the existing component rather than changing its mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 presents a history-aware streaming reconstruction framework as its primary contribution. V2 redefines the central contribution as a reusable Fuse-and-Refine module for existing feed-forward Gaussian models, emphasizing redundancy reduction and flexible primitive placement, with streaming as an application. Static-only training, interactive speed, and strong static/dynamic reconstruction claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations concerning pixel-aligned redundancy, constrained primitive placement, and why learned refinement improves upon heuristic fusion. It interprets the new temporal controls and explicitly limits gains when initial primitives are poor or camera baselines are large. The conclusion replaces v1's emphasis on repeated per-frame reconstruction and high-resolution scalability with these input-quality limits and persistent dynamic-region warping artifacts.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link, component runtime details, an A100 timing comparison, and concrete retraining details for the DepthSplat extension. Most architecture, optimizer, training-budget, voxel-grid, and tracking parameters were already supplied in v1's appendix. The PDFs alone do not establish whether the new project link provides downloadable code.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against learned Gaussian graph, voxel, and point-based methods, including Gaussian Graph Network, SCube, EvolSplat, and Splatformer. It also discusses point-voxel processing networks and heuristic Gaussian merging, while shortening earlier dynamic-scene and animation coverage. This changes the research context beyond citation updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around fusion and refinement. V2 introduces reconstruction preliminaries, separates the general module from its streaming application, moves detailed streaming mathematics into the appendix, and adds a societal-impact section.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two-column to single-column formatting, adds a dedicated Fuse-and-Refine diagram and several experimental tables, and restructures existing tables. The original streaming overview, teaser, and close-ups move to the appendix; earlier qualitative grids and the convergence plot remain. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical justification for learned refinement. The new temporal-fusion controls, camera-count tests, Gaussian Graph Network comparison, and DepthSplat integration address v1's limited evidence about alternative fusion strategies and applicability beyond its original configuration. Runtime breakdowns and more specific failure conditions also make the claims easier to assess. The DepthSplat test remains small and statistical uncertainty is still unreported, but the added validation provides a clear substantial net improvement.
